''Matthew. S. Paul &c.''}}{{hwe|thevv|Matthevv}}, S. Paul: becau{{ls}}e it is {{ls}}o neither in Greeke nor Latin. though in the toppes of the leaues folovving, where vve may be bolder, we adde, S. Matthevv & c. to {{ls}}atisfie the reader. Much vnlike to the Prote{{ls}}tants our Aduer{{ls}}aries, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Bib. an.'' 1579. 1580. ''an.'' 1577 1562.}}vvhich make no {{ls}}cruple to leaue out the name of Paul in the title of the Epi{{ls}}tle to the Hebrues, though it be in euery Greeke booke vvhich they tran{{ls}}late. And their mo{{ls}}t authori{{ls}}ed Engli{{ls}}h Bibles leaue out (Catholike) in the title of S. Iames Epi{{ls}}tle and the re{{ls}}t, vvhich vvere famou{{ls}}ly knovven in the primitiue Church by the name of ''Catholicæ Epi{{ls}}tolæ.'' Eu{{ls}}eb. hi{{ls}}t. Eccl. li. 2 c. 22.

{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=An other reading in the margent.}}Item vve giue the Reader in places of {{ls}}ome importance, an other reading in the margent, {{ls}}pecially vvhen the Greeke is agreable to the {{ls}}ame. as Io. 4. ''tran{{ls}}iet de morte ad vitam. Other Latin copies haue, tran{{ls}}iit, and {{ls}}o it is in the Greeke.''

Vve binde not our {{ls}}elues to the pointes of any one copie, print, or edition of the vulgar Latin, in places of no controuer{{ls}}ie, but folovv the pointing mo{{ls}}t {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The pointing {{ls}}ometime altered.}} agreable to the Greeke and to the fathers commentaries. As Col. 1, 10. ''Ambulantes dignè Deo, per omnia placentes.'' Vvalking vvorthy of God, in al things plea{{ls}}ing. ἀξίως τοῦ κυρίου εἰς πᾶσαν ἀρέσκειαν. Eph. 1, 17. Vve point thus, ''Deus Domini no{{ls}}tri Ie{{ls}}u Chri{{ls}}ti, pater gloriæ.'' as in the Greeke, and S. Chry{{ls}}o{{ls}}tom, & S. Hierom both in text and commentaries. Vvhich the Catholike reader {{ls}}pecially mu{{ls}}t marke, le{{ls}}t he finde fault, vvhen he {{ls}}eeth our tran{{ls}}lation di{{ls}}agree in {{ls}}uch places from the pointing of his Latin Te{{ls}}tament.

{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The margent reading {{ls}}ometime preferred before the text.}}Vve tran{{ls}}late {{ls}}ometime the word that is in the Latin margent, and not that in the text, when by the Greeke or the fathers we {{ls}}ee it is a manife{{ls}}t fault of the writers heretofore, that mi{{ls}}tooke one word for an other. As, ''In fine, not, in fide, 1. Pet. 3. v. 8. præ{{ls}}entiam, not, præ{{ls}}cientiam, 2 Pet. 1. v. 16. Heb. 13. latuerunt, not, placuerunt.''

Thus we haue endeuoured by al meanes to {{ls}}atisfie the indifferent reader, and to helpe his vnder{{ls}}tanding euery way, both in the text, and by Annotations: and withal to deale mo{{ls}}t {{ls}}incerely before God and man, in tran{{ls}}lating and expounding the mo{{ls}}t {{ls}}acred text of the holy Te{{ls}}tament. Fare wel good Reader, and if we profit the any whit by our poore paines let vs for Gods {{ls}}ake be partakers of thy deuout praiers, & together with humble and contrite hart call vpō our Sauiour Chri{{ls}}t to cea{{ls}}e the{{ls}}e troubles & {{ls}}tormes of his dere{{ls}}t {{ls}}pou{{ls}}e: in the meane time comforting our {{ls}}elues with this {{ls}}aying of S. Augu{{ls}}tine: ''That Heretikes, vvhen they receiue povver corporally to afflict the Church, doe exerci{{ls}}e her patience: but vvhen they oppugne her onely by their euil doctrine or opinions, then they exerci{{ls}}e her vvi{{ls}}edom.'' De ciuit. Dei li. 18. ca. 51.<noinclude></noinclude>
